newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Pope to beatify Guatemala nun in first for Centam.
newsitem.headline: Pope to beatify Guatemala nun in first for Centam.

text.p: A 19th-century nun who promoted education for women and fled an anti-Catholic regime in Guatemala will become the first Central American-born person to be beatified, church sources said.
Beatification is the final step before sainthood.

The Pope, in a Vatican ceremony on Sunday, is scheduled to beatify Mother Encarnacion Rosal, of the religious order of Bethlemite Sisters. She was born in 1820 in Guatemala's second largest city, Quetzaltenango, followers of Rosal said.
"She will be the first Central American, male or female, to be beatified," Ana Isabela Villalobos, a Bethlemite sister, told Reuters in a recent interview.
"She had to abandon Guatemala precisely because she was a forward-thinking woman who was the first to concern herself with education for women in Guatemala," Villalobos said.
In the 1870s an anti-Catholic movement swept Guatemala and then-President Justo Rufino Barrios prohibited religious work.

The Sacred Heart School that Rosal had founded in Quetzaltenango was forced to close its doors in 1873. Rosal and other members of her order hid out in private houses until they fled in 1877 to Costa Rica, where Rosal founded another school.

But another anti-religious movement forced her to move to Colombia where she opened an orphanage and another school. She died in 1886 in Ecuador after she fell off a horse. Her body is buried in Colombia.
Rosal, who left an autobiography and a collection of letters documenting her life, shifted the emphasis of the order to education and opened Sunday schools for maids.

"She's considered our reformer because she saw the needs of promoting women's education. She taught young women of that era not only household crafts, but also literature, writing, geography, French, English and astronomy," Villalobos said.
The Bethlemites returned to Guatemala in 1955 after more than 75 years of exile and now have 30 sisters who run schools and social programmes for the poor.
